blocks.text: …in harmony with dog and nature
Definition and purpose 🐕
The team walk is the way to deepen the relationship between us and our dog.
The team walk is understood as a way of being together in nature that suits the dog.

We learn to lead our dog in such a way that we can be out and about relaxed and largely independent of the situation. In doing so, we achieve a noticeable reduction in conflicts and a clear expansion of our comfort zone when leading the dog.
The team walk is the way to deepen the relationship between us and our dog.
The team walk is understood as a way of being together in nature that suits the dog.

We learn to lead our dog in such a way that we can be out and about relaxed and largely independent of the situation – with a noticeable reduction in conflicts and a clear expansion of our comfort zone.
Suitable places and progression 🌲
As often as possible, we take our dog out into open countryside away from urban areas. Ideally, we move through forest, grassland or, alternatively, spacious parks and green spaces.
At first, it should be extensive terrain with little foot traffic. The more remote the place, the more suitable it is.
As routine grows, we may gradually include livelier places. The progression is guided by our steadily growing calm in leading our dog and by its balance when it is with us.
Approach in the terrain 🐾
We go into the terrain with our dog without time pressure. It is important that we carry neither a fixed destination nor a planned route in our minds.
We walk calmly through the terrain, step by step. We leave at home all things and thoughts that could distract us. Every single step together with our dog tells a story.

As often and as far as is possible and permitted, we leave the main paths and move through off-the-beaten-track terrain on trails and quiet side paths. Of course, we respect the resting areas of wild animals and move considerately around plants.
Mindful walking and perception 👁️
We walk calmly and mindfully, step by step. We feel the wind, hear the birdsong and notice the ground beneath us. The dog already does this and is therefore constantly ahead of us in knowledge.
We walk in calm and are fully present with our senses. Over time, our dog adopts the calm way we walk and adapts to it.
Every now and then we pause to observe our surroundings attentively. We use all our senses and do as our dog does. We smell, hear, see and feel everything that comes in on us.
Development and progress 📈
At the beginning, we will become acquainted with restlessness in ourselves and in our dog. We are not used to settling into the calm of a thinker.

Over the days and weeks of our training, however, we will feel a growing calm, which then gradually takes hold in our dog as well. Depending on the character of our dog, this happens in very individual forms and over different lengths of time.

Once we have completed our rounds through the terrain with our dog in the team walk for some time and have allowed the necessary calm to settle in ourselves, we can turn to the scouting techniques in the next section.
Important notes ⚠️
We avoid moving through the terrain loudly and quickly.
We avoid doing the team walk under time pressure or within a defined time window.
We avoid planning the route in advance.
We avoid all distraction.
We avoid hectic, unconscious behaviour.
Practical impulse: Simply be there

Leave your phone at home, plan no route and set yourself no goal. Go out with your dog – and, in your mind, follow him for a moment. What does he perceive? What does he smell? This awareness is the core of the team walk and the beginning of a deeper connection.
→ Does our dog know “sit” and “down” reliably?
→ In the beginning, am I training in terrain free of distraction?
→ Have I ensured an undisturbed session?
→ Am I training consistently on the long line for the first period?
→ Am I increasing the training demands step by step towards use in situations with distraction?
→ Do I only switch to off-leash training once the leash is no longer needed to carry out the exercise?
→ Do I communicate with the dog calmly and reliably?
→ Is my body work right, and do I walk confidently towards the dog?
→ Do I bring the dog into the “down” confidently and promptly?
→ Do I regularly let the dog stay in position for a while?
→ Do I end the exercise calmly, following the instructions and with appropriate pauses?
→ Do I praise generously afterwards?
